items.title: Find out when mail delivery will stop coming to your Mississauga home
items.summary: Thousands of Mississauga households will eventually have to walk to a community mailbox to collect their mail as Canada Post moves ahead with plans to end traditional door-to-door delivery across much of the city. The transition is part of a nationwide effort to overhaul Canada Post’s operations, with the Crown Corporation planning to convert approximately four million addresses that still receive mail at their front doors to community mailboxes over the next five years. For Mississauga residents, the changes will begin in 2027, with additional neighbourhoods scheduled to make the switch in 2028. The rollout is organized by the first three characters of postal codes, so residents can estimate when their neighbourhood will be affected without waiting for a letter from Canada Post. Here is what Mississauga residents need to know about the changes, including when their home delivery is expected to end, why Canada Post is making the move and what alternatives are available for seniors and people with disabilities. When will community mailboxes arrive in Mississauga? According to the schedule, Mississauga neighbourhoods will be divided into four conversion periods between October 2027 and November 2028. The first changes are expected in October 2027, when homes with postal codes beginning with L5M and L5N will transition to community mailboxes.

items.title: Speed cameras were removed from roads across Mississauga one year ago
items.summary: It’s been one year since automated speed enforcement cameras last captured images of cars speeding on roads in Mississauga and across Ontario. The 22 roadside cameras that had been set up at various locations in Mississauga snapped their final photos of lead-footed drivers and their vehicles on Nov. 13, 2025. The provincial government banned the devices across Ontario, effective Nov. 14, 2025, in a controversial move that drew significant opposition from the City of Mississauga and other municipalities. The speed enforcement program had been successful in reducing the number of serious and fatal collisions, Mississauga and other cities argued. However, Ontario Premier Doug Ford, who’d called the speed cameras a “cash grab,” and his government weren’t convinced by opponents of the ban. The ban did away with more than 700 ASE roadside devices that had been deployed since 2019 in 40 municipalities. The cameras were decommissioned in accordance with the provincial government’s Bill 56, also known as the Building a More Competitive Economy Act, which passed on Oct. 30, 2025. “The loss of speed cameras will have a significant impact and place added pressure on our existing road safety initiatives,” Sam Rogers, Mississauga’s commissioner of transportation and works, said last November as the ban took effect.

items.title: Ward 2 and Ward 7 Get New Faces as Mississauga's 2026-2030 Council Takes Oaths Nov. 16
items.summary: Mississauga's newly elected city council will be sworn in at an inaugural meeting on Nov. 16, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo, who is moving up from the Ward 2 council seat, will take his oath of office alongside two first-time councillors and nine returning members for the 2026-2030 term. Tom Ellard will take over the Ward 2 seat Tedjo is vacating, while Lucas Alves succeeds Dipika Damerla in Ward 7 after she ran unsuccessfully for mayor, insauga.com said. The meeting is open to the public on a first-come, first-seated basis, according to the report. Two days later, on Nov. 18, the new council will hold its first general committee meeting to begin addressing city business, the outlet noted. The council's term runs until late 2030.

items.title: Mississauga Diwali Fireworks Complaints Drop to 236, Still Draw 25 Fines
items.summary: The City of Mississauga received 236 public complaints about Diwali fireworks between Nov. 6 and the end of Nov. 9, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that bylaw officers issued 25 fines for fireworks-related violations during that stretch of the five-day festival, which concluded on Nov. 10. A city spokesperson told insauga.com the fines included penalties for selling fireworks without a city licence and for selling roman candles. Insauga.com noted the city has not said whether additional complaints came in on the festival's final day. This year's total is a steep drop from the 432 complaints logged during Diwali in 2025, which the city had called the highest in its history, according to the report. Brampton, meanwhile, issued $37,500 in fines after about 760 of its 1,688 service requests over the same period involved fireworks, insauga.com said.

items.title: Search Warrant at Mississauga Home Turns Up Six of Nine Coffee Machines Stolen in July Heist
items.summary: Peel Regional Police have arrested two men in connection with the theft of nine high-end commercial coffee machines worth an estimated $85,955 from a Mississauga business, according to a police news release. Police said officers first responded to a break-and-enter at a commercial building on the morning of July 11, and investigators later determined the machines had been listed for sale on an online marketplace. On Nov. 1, police executed a search warrant at a residence near Bloor Street and Fieldgate Drive and recovered six of the nine stolen machines, the release said. Investigators believe the remaining three machines had already been sold online. Police charged Cezary Szuc, 45, and Leslie Ayotte, 57, both of Mississauga, with possession of property obtained by crime. Both men were released on undertakings and are scheduled to appear in court at a later date, according to police. The allegations have not been proven in court.
